# Datathon Project 

## Datathon components 

2 assessed aspects 

  1. Report (50% of overall mark)
  2. Recorded presentation (40% of overall mark)

## Datathon projects 

Create a **data story** using OECD Health Data 

* Entirely up to you to decide on your data story 
  - Specific variables & covariates (dates, countries, demographics, etc.) are entirely up to you! 
* You are invited to use other datasets, but must use some data from the [health care utilisation dataset](https://data-explorer.oecd.org/vis?df%5Bds%5D=DisseminateFinalDMZ&df%5Bid%5D=DSD_HEALTH_PROC%40DF_KEY_INDIC&df%5Bag%5D=OECD.ELS.HD&dq=.................&pd=,&to%5BTIME_PERIOD%5D=false&vw=ov)

## {#slide25-id data-menu-title="Data Story vs Story with Data" background-image="images/DataStory_StorywithData.png" background-size="contain"}

## 🥪 Data Story vs 🍕 Story with Data 

* Datathon = 🥪 **data story – the foundation is data & data is revealing the story**
* The narrative explains and contextualizes the data, making the findings accessible, understandable & engaging
* Data stories are about inspiring change & clear, data-driven calls to action
* You can read more about this distinction on [Brent Dykes effectivestorytelling blog](https://www.effectivedatastorytelling.com/post/data-stories-vs-stories-with-data-whats-the-difference)

## {#slide26-id data-menu-title="Lydia Hooper's Data Story Framing" .smaller}

::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="70%"}

![](images/Hooper_DataStorytelling.jpeg){.lightbox}

:::

:::{.column width="30%"}

You can read [Lydia Hooper’s blog here](https://venngage.com/blog/data-storytelling/). 

Note that data storytelling and stories with data are used interchangeably in the blog post, but what is discussed is what we are calling data stories. 

:::
:::::

## Things to consider *before* narrative and visualisations 

* Who is your audience? 
* What do you need your audience to know or do?
* How will you communicate to your audience? (e.g., written report, presentation)
* 🥪 Data drives the story. You are not looking for data to support a narrative you have already decided on 

## Storyboarding can help! 

* **Do not start with presentation software** when creating a data story 
  - your presentation is a final product - not a work in progress 
* **Storyboard** can be used to establish a structure & flow for your narrative
  - a **visual outline** of the content you plan to develop 
  - particularly useful when working in online &/or in teams

## {#slide31-id data-menu-title="Example of student storyboard" background-image="images/Ex_storyboard.png" footer="false"}

## Storytelling techniques {.smaller}

::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}

1. **Lead statement**

* Complete sentence 
* Conveys the problem and articulates key insight

:::

::: {.column width="50%"}

2. **Elevator pitch**

* Short statements encapsulating your data story which captures your audience’s attention and sparks interest 
* 5 steps 
  - Understand your objective 
  - Understand your audience 
  - Outline the problem 
  - Outline the solution 
  - Call to action   

:::
:::::

## 🗝️ Key features of a good pitch: 

* Credible (no overblown claims) 
* Customised to your audience 
  - you’ll rarely give a pitch to the same audience twice 
* Conversational for non-expert audience (avoid jargon) 
* Clear 
* Concise 
 
## 💡💡 Pitch top tips 💡💡

* Content, structure, delivery: all **equally** important 
* Attention-grabbing start and solid conclusion 
* Audience – language 
* Have some notes, but don’t read from a script 
* Thinking pauses. You need to breathe. The audience needs to think about what you are saying (we speak 135-150 words/minute at a natural pace). 
* Use your own voice. Helps with credibility
